raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
…workers

With --tokenizer-worker-num N > 1 every worker ran the fast image processor on the serving GPU and opened its own CUDA context next to the scheduler's static memory pool. On a 32 GB GPU with 16 workers, concurrent image requests failed with CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY or CUDA_ERROR_ALREADY_ACQUIRED and HTTP 500. Several workers now leave the fast processor on the CPU, where they are real preprocessing parallelism; a single worker keeps the GPU path

Enabled on NVIDIA GPUs only (is_cuda()), where it was measured; other devices keep the previous behavior.

Assisted-by: Claude

+    def _many_tokenizer_workers(self) -> bool:
+        """Whether several tokenizer worker processes each run this processor.
+
+        Each worker that ran the fast image processor on the GPU would open its
+        own CUDA context next to the scheduler's static memory pool; with 16
+        workers on a 32 GB GPU image requests then fail with CUDA out-of-memory
+        or "device busy" errors. Those workers preprocess on the CPU instead,
+        where they are also real parallelism. Validated on NVIDIA GPUs only;
+        other devices keep their placement.
+        """
+        return _is_cuda and getattr(self.server_args, "tokenizer_worker_num", 1) > 1
+
     def _preprocessing_competes_with_the_scheduler(self) -> bool:
         """Whether image preprocessing contends with the serving accelerator.
 
@@ -764,7 +778,7 @@ def _preprocessing_competes_with_the_scheduler(self) -> bool:
         """
         if _is_cpu or get_exec().deterministic.rl_on_policy_target is not None:
             return False
-        if self.disable_fast_image_processor:
+        if self.disable_fast_image_processor or self._many_tokenizer_workers():
             return False
         image_processor = getattr(self._processor, "image_processor", None)
         if not isinstance(image_processor, BaseImageProcessor):

-            if not platform.is_cuda_alike():

+class TestSeveralTokenizerWorkers(CustomTestCase):
+    """Several tokenizer workers preprocess on the CPU: on the GPU each would
+    open its own CUDA context next to the scheduler's memory pool (CUDA out of
+    memory under concurrent image requests)."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        reset_context()
+        self.addCleanup(reset_context)
+
+    def _processor(self, tokenizer_worker_num):
+        from transformers import BaseImageProcessor
+
+        processor = _make(base_gpu_id=3, tokenizer_worker_num=tokenizer_worker_num)
+        processor.disable_fast_image_processor = False
+        processor._processor = SimpleNamespace(image_processor=BaseImageProcessor())
+        return processor
+
+    def _cuda(self, nvidia=True):
+        platforms = SimpleNamespace(
+            current_platform=SimpleNamespace(
+                is_cuda_alike=lambda: True, device_type="cuda"
+            )
+        )
+        return patch.multiple(
+            BASE,
+            platforms=platforms,
+            _is_cpu=False,
+            _is_cuda=nvidia,
+            _is_xpu=False,
+            _is_npu=False,
+        )
+
+    def test_device_is_left_unset(self):
+        with self._cuda():
+            one = self._processor(1)._fast_image_processor_device(_Processor())
+            several = self._processor(8)._fast_image_processor_device(_Processor())
+        self.assertEqual(one, "cuda:3")
+        self.assertIsNone(several)
+
+    def test_other_cuda_alike_devices_keep_the_gpu_placement(self):
+        # e.g. ROCm: only validated on NVIDIA GPUs, so unchanged elsewhere.
+        with self._cuda(nvidia=False):
+            several = self._processor(8)._fast_image_processor_device(_Processor())
+        self.assertEqual(several, "cuda:3")
+
+    def test_preprocessing_no_longer_competes_with_the_scheduler(self):
+        with self._cuda():
+            one = self._processor(1)._preprocessing_competes_with_the_scheduler()
+            several = self._processor(8)._preprocessing_competes_with_the_scheduler()
+        self.assertTrue(one)
+        self.assertFalse(several)
+
